The plan in one screen

Three things shape every route

Bangladeshi MBBS (2019–20 session), results out September 2026, internship from Oct–Nov 2026 in Chattogram, no work experience, USD 30k budget. Long-term goal: practise medicine in the US. Fields: public health, epidemiology, global health, clinical research, aerospace medicine.

  1. 1

    Finish the internship

    Without it there is no full BMDC registration, so no FCPS, full GMC, Saudi, Qatar or UAE licence, and no AHPRA registration. Realistic time to leave: December 2027 to April 2028.

  2. 2

    Best bridge to the US

    Take Step 1 during the internship, then a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK, aiming for the 2029 Match. That keeps the graduation recent (about 3 years) and earns US letters of recommendation.

  3. 3

    Apply now, start later

    Erasmus Mundus, Gates Cambridge, KAUST, MEXT, GKS, Stipendium Hungaricum, Türkiye and CSC need no work experience. Most 2027 starts collide with the internship, so ask each programme about late arrival or aim for 2028.

Timeline from now to the 2029 Match

  1. Nov 2026 – Jan 2027 Now

    The application wave

    Funded master's and PhD deadlines cluster here. One master motivation letter, adapted per programme.

  2. Nov 2026 – late 2027

    Internship year

    Unlocks full BMDC registration — the key to every licence route.

  3. 2027

    USMLE Step 1

    Sit it during the internship. Decide on PLAB 1 before Dhaka sittings end in Feb 2027.

  4. Dec 2027 – Apr 2028

    Departure window

    Internship done. Start a funded degree, or a paid research post abroad.

  5. 2028

    US research job + Step 2 CK

    J-1 Research Scholar or H-1B cap-exempt post. US letters. ECFMG Pathway + OET.

  6. March 2029 Goal

    The Match

    Graduation still recent, US experience in hand.

    Open portal for Paid US research post (J-1 or H-1B cap-exempt) (opens in a new tab) ↗
    Read the story about Paid US research post (J-1 or H-1B cap-exempt) →
    Full notes & source

    The fastest real exit and the best bridge to a US Match: US letters and recent graduation. Avoid unpaid posts. Visa: J-1 research scholar is safest (ECFMG can sponsor if the host can't). H-1B $100k fee: Proclamation 11069 (18 Sep 2026) extends it to 21 Sep 2027, but a California court vacated the agency policies applying it on 30 Sep (government appealed to the 9th Circuit, 9 Oct) and a Massachusetts ruling also blocks it; appeals pending in the 1st, 9th and D.C. Circuits; as of 15 Oct no court had stayed the rulings (law-firm summaries; dockets not verified). The DHS $103,265 proposal's comment period closed 24 Sep with no final rule. DHS proposed (25 Aug 2026) an extra $103,265 fee for cap-subject petitions only — cap-exempt university employers wouldn't pay it. J-1 'duration of status' rule postponed by a court on 14 Sep. Keep his online presence clean before a J-1 interview. 1 Nov: no new court ruling found; university ISSS guidance (7 Oct) still says the fee is not being collected.

    Official source for Paid US research post (J-1 or H-1B cap-exempt) (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 1 Nov 2026

    Open portal for USMLE + ECFMG certification (opens in a new tab) ↗
    Read the story about USMLE + ECFMG certification →
    Full notes & source

    Step 1 and Step 2 CK plus a Pathway (OET Medicine) are required; with no licence, Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) is the realistic one. IMGs now apply for USMLE via FSMB (since 12 Jan 2026). Step 2 CK is the score screen. Check the school's ECFMG Sponsor Note on wdoms.org. NRMP 2027 Match: registration opened 15 Sep 2026 (multi-factor login now mandatory), registration deadline 29 Jan 2027, ECFMG requirements due by the rank-list deadline 3 Mar 2027, Match Day 19 Mar 2027 — too early for him; target 2028 or 2029. Policy: the 75-country immigrant-visa pause (Bangladesh included) is no longer in effect since 21 Aug 2026 (court order in CLINIC v. Rubio) — good news for a later green card, but litigation continues. The DHS rule ending J-1 'duration of status' (due 15 Sep 2026) was postponed by a court; ECFMG is watching. As of 1 Nov the only recent ECFMG news post is still the D/S postponement (23 Sep); no 2028 Pathways, OET or fee news. NRMP published three new transition-to-residency data reports on 14 Oct (no rule change). USMLE now uses new software with 30-minute blocks (Step 1: 14 × 30 min since 14 May 2026; Step 2 CK: 16 × 30 min since 7 May 2026) — practise with the new tutorial. Bangladesh is not on the US travel-ban list. NRMP's Oct 2026 Illuminator: programs must give applicants at least 48 hours to answer interview invitations and can't over-invite; a voluntary rank-list lock pilot runs in IM, Pediatrics and Vascular Surgery — no IMG-specific rule change.

    Official source for USMLE + ECFMG certification (opens in a new tab) ↗Verified 1 Nov 2026

    Medical Training (Prioritisation) Act: regulations laid 15 Sep 2026 for training posts starting in 2027 give priority at both shortlisting and offer to UK, Irish and EEA-EFTA graduates, doctors who completed UK Foundation or the prior training stage, and British citizens / ILR / settled status holders. A fresh IMG on a visa is not prioritised, so PLAB now leads mainly to non-training (trust-grade) jobs first. Registration must be applied for within 2 years of passing PLAB 2. Immigration rules HC 584 (stages 8 Oct, 29 Oct, 30 Nov, 9 Dec 2026) amend Skilled Worker — details not verified; Graduate route drops to 18 months from 1 Jan 2027. Ireland's Medical Council now accepts a PLAB 2 pass in place of PRES (confirmed 24 Oct), so PLAB also opens Ireland. HC 584 Skilled Worker changes from 8 Oct are mainly about modern-slavery victims and sponsor rules — nothing doctor-specific found. GMC (gmc-uk.org news, announced May 2026): PLAB 1 will no longer be held in Dhaka from February 2027 (also Alexandria, Accra, Chennai); overseas sittings drop from four to three a year. After that he must sit PLAB 1 in another country (e.g. one of the remaining Indian centres) or in the UK — extra visa and travel cost.

Estimated application fees

Tick routes above to add them up.

Amounts are in each school's own currency. The first SOPHAS programme costs $155 and each extra one $65. Hopkins, Emory, the Emory MPH and Columbia all share one SOPHAS application. Several fees are waivable (Oxford for Bangladesh, SOPHAS on request, MBZUAI at 75%+), so treat this as a ceiling.

How to read it. 0 means no funded route exists. 1–2 is a long shot: elite schemes with a few dozen awards, usually won by people with research records. 3 is an outside chance worth a strong application. Open any route for the four-factor breakdown and what would raise the score.

The pattern. Nothing scores above 4 right now. The best odds are the government schemes where Bangladesh is a partner (Stipendium Hungaricum, CSC) and the health-focused Erasmus Mundus programmes. The biggest levers are the same everywhere: a class-rank certificate, one research output during the internship, and applying to intakes you can actually start (January 2028 or later).

Unanswered

Open questions that decide several routes

Each one is worth an email. The answer can open or close several routes at once.

  1. When is the MBBS conferred?

    Before or only after the internship? It decides SpaceMed, Commonwealth Shared, Maastricht and others that need the degree finished by a deadline.

  2. Maastricht admission route

    Bachelor's route (GRE needed) or bachelor's + master's route (no GRE)? Does his average convert to at least 7.5/10? Ask masteradmission-fhml@maastrichtuniversity.nl.

  3. Swedish Institute's 3,000 hours

    Paid or freelance work separate from the internship, before Feb 2027. The SI FAQ says internships don't count.

  4. Hopkins work-experience line

    The one-year line appears on the ScM page, not the PhD page. Ask BSPH.EpiAcademic@jh.edu whether the internship counts.

  5. MBBS → direct PhD in Australia and NZ

    No university says an MBBS alone qualifies. It's case by case (publications, research), with an MPhil as fallback.

  6. WES timing

    Starting in early November lands mid-December — too late for a verified 1 Dec file. Ask Hopkins and Emory if WES can follow.

Round 1 has closed: round 2 on 11 Jan, and only with a supervisor

The Imperial College President's PhD Scholarships are the most prestigious doctoral funding Imperial offers. They're fully funded and a real route into world-class research. Round 1 closed on 2 Nov, so the live chance is round 2 on 11 Jan 2027, and without a supervisor's agreement you're not ready for it.

Before you board

PortalImperial online application (via the scheme page) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Imperial states there is no application fee for PhDs (taught master's cost £90). No separate scholarship form: apply for the PhD place and select the President's PhD Scholarship in the funding section; the department then nominates you.

How this was checked: Fee quote from Imperial's postgraduate admissions page (Muse, 2 Nov). The scheme page rendered blank for a live re-read, so dates and stipend come from the board's weekly sweep.

01

What it pays

  • Full tuition fees at the overseas rate.
  • £27,036 a year tax-free stipend for up to 3.5 years, plus £2,000 a year for research costs.
  • About 50 awards a year, open to any nationality.
  • Your $30,000 budget stays untouched: it can go to USMLE fees and US clinical experience instead.

02

Who can apply

  • Any nationality, Bangladesh included.
  • A first-class degree or equivalent. How Imperial reads an MBBS comes down to your marks and class rank.
  • A supervisor's agreement first: find a faculty member in an area like the School of Public Health, email them your CV and a short proposal, and get their yes before you apply.

03

Dates that matter

  • Round 1: closed 2 Nov 2026 (decisions by 31 Jan 2027).
  • Round 2: 11 Jan 2027. Round 3: 1 Mar 2027.
  • Funded 2027–28 places can start as late as 1 Nov 2027, which brushes against the end of your internship.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD from Imperial in public health makes you exceptionally competitive for academic residency programmes, and London gives you a base for PLAB and NHS contacts. But the plan that works for 2029 is Step 1 during the internship, a paid US research job, then Step 2 CK. A 3.5-year PhD replaces that plan rather than adding to it, and your Match year moves to roughly 2031–32.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timing

    Round 1 has closed. Round 2 on 11 Jan 2027 is the realistic target, and you need an agreed supervisor before then.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: competition

    Fifty awards across the whole college, usually for people with research experience. A fresh MBBS with no publications needs a strong supervisor connection.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: years since graduation

    Many US programmes screen on how long ago you graduated. A PhD explains the gap well for academic programmes, less so for community ones.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: clinical distance

    Three and a half years in a research group means arranging observerships before you reapply to residency.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat this as a physician-scientist route, not a 2029 route. Apply in round 2 if a supervisor commits in the next two months. Otherwise keep your energy on Step 1 and a paid US research post.

Brilliant funding, wrong field for epidemiology

OIST is an elite, English-language graduate university on Okinawa with one of the most generous PhD packages anywhere. It's basic science and computation rather than public health, so the question is whether you'd want a lab life for five years.

Before you board

PortalOIST graduate school application ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Non-refundable, and OIST offers no waivers for personal financial situations. Check a supervisor has room for students before you apply.

How this was checked: Confirmed live on oist.jp/admissions/phd-program/apply-phd (2 Nov 2026).

01

What it is

A single 5-year integrated PhD. The first two years are lab rotations and coursework, and the last three are thesis research. There are no departments: units cover molecular and cell biology, neuroscience, mathematics and computation, chemistry, physics and ecology.

02

What it pays

  • Tuition included, with a stipend of about ¥2.6 million a year, rising to about ¥3.6 million.
  • Support for relocation and conference travel.
  • Cost to apply: ¥5,000, non-refundable and without waivers. It's small, but it isn't free.

03

Who can apply

  • Completion of a bachelor's, master's or equivalent before the admission date. Medicine isn't named, so confirm with admissions that an MBBS is accepted.
  • Check that your chosen unit actually has room to supervise new PhD students. OIST warns that strong applicants are rejected when the field has no space.

04

Dates that matter

  • 15 Nov 2026, 23:59 JST for the 2027 admissions workshop round.
  • Entry on 1 May or 1 Sep 2027, or 1 Jan 2028. The January 2028 entry is the one that fits the end of your internship.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD with strong papers helps for academic residencies, but US programmes weigh clinical experience and clinical research more heavily than bench work. Europe's licensing routes (PLAB, the German Kenntnisprüfung, Ireland's PRES) don't change at all.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timeline

    Starting in 2028 and finishing five years later puts a US Match at roughly 2033.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: field mismatch

    There is no public health or epidemiology unit. Computational biology is your closest door.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: admission

    Research experience matters a lot, and you'd be competing with people who have lab degrees.

07

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you're deliberately choosing a research career and would lean into computational work. For a Match-focused plan, skip it.

01

What it is

A 1+3 model. In year one you do three short rotations in different labs plus taught modules, then choose your main project. The degree is awarded by the University of Cambridge, and you work on the Wellcome Genome Campus.

02

What it pays

  • Full university tuition fees and a stipend (£25,270 in year one at Oct 2025 rates).
  • Visa and NHS surcharge costs reimbursed.
  • At least 12 funded studentships, whatever your nationality.
  • Cost to apply: nothing for the Sanger application. If selected, the Cambridge admission application costs £20.

03

Who can apply

  • Candidates expected to hold a 1st or good 2:1, or an equivalent overseas qualification. Whether your MBBS is read that way is worth asking.
  • Genomics and data science are the focus. Basic Python or R and some statistics will help an MBBS profile a lot.

04

Dates that matter

  • 24 Nov 2026, 09:00 GMT is the closing time.
  • Start is in October 2027, which is likely to collide with your internship: ask whether a later start is possible before spending time on the application.

05

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Cambridge-linked PhD with strong genomics papers is a great physician-scientist credential and can put you in contact with US collaborators for letters. It doesn't give you US clinical experience, and a four-year PhD moves a Match to around 2032.

06

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: scope

    This is genomics and computation, not general public health.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: preparation

    Selection favours people with coding or lab skills you may not have built yet.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: clinical distance

    Four years away from patients means rebuilding clinical credibility afterwards.

07

The honest recommendation

If genomic epidemiology really pulls you, ask Sanger about starting later and whether an MBBS qualifies, and spend the internship building Python and R skills. If the 2029 Match is the priority, this isn't the route.

What it pays

  • About 60 awards, based on merit rather than financial need.

Who can apply

  • A Master's application to ETH for the autumn semester, with a thesis pre-proposal you write yourself. That pre-proposal carries a lot of weight.
  • Typical English requirement is around IELTS 7.0 or TOEFL 100; check your programme's page.

03

Dates that matter

  • The window is 1–30 Nov 2026, with a September 2027 start. That start collides with the internship, so ask about a later one or plan for the next cycle.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

An ETH MSc in health sciences, statistics or biomedical engineering looks excellent on a residency application, and it links to aerospace physiology research. What it can't do is give you US clinical experience or any shortcut to practise in Switzerland or the EU, where you'd still need the local recognition exams and the language.

  2. 02

  3. 03

    Catch 3: timeline

    One and a half to two years away from the USMLE track pushes a Match to about 2031.

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you want a quantitative research career and can write a convincing thesis pre-proposal. For a clinical Match, skip it. For European practice, Germany's Kenntnisprüfung or the UK's PLAB are more direct.

01

What it pays

  • Full course fees plus a living grant for the whole degree.
  • A MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology carries overseas fees of about £36,900 (2027–28), so funding it yourself isn't realistic.

02

Who can apply

  • Any nationality, any subject. Medicine degrees are accepted.
  • The course deadline is what counts: everyone who applies by it and gets an offer is considered.
  • Skip the MSc in International Health and Tropical Medicine: it asks for 3+ years of low-resource work experience, which you don't have yet.

03

  • 1 Dec 2026, 12:00 UK for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology. The Oxford and NDPH pages served older-cycle text on re-check, so confirm on the Graduate Admissions page.
  • An October 2027 start collides with the internship. The next realistic cycle is December 2027 for October 2028.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A one-year Oxford MSc in epidemiology is the strongest version of an academic credential you can get quickly, and Oxford's population-health groups have US collaborations that can lead to letters. It's still not US clinical experience, and in the UK it doesn't replace PLAB.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: competition

    You can't apply to Clarendon directly. You need a place first, and marks and rank near the top.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: timing

    The cycle that fits your internship is next year's.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: exam clash

    An Oxford MSc plus Step 2 CK preparation in the same year is a heavy load.

06

The honest recommendation

Apply for the MSc in Global Health Science & Epidemiology only if you can get a later start or are happy to wait for the 2028 intake. Use the waiver, and never pay course fees from your $30,000.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: USAJobs for federal posts, university career pages for the rest ↗ (opens in a new tab)

There is no application fee for searching or applying to these posts. Posts are advertised employer by employer (USAJobs for federal posts, university and hospital career pages, NIH institute pages). Costs start only at the visa stage: if ECFMG sponsors your J-1, that is a $370 annual fee, $220 SEVIS and the J-1 visa fee (see the ECFMG J-1 card).

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against ECFMG's EVSP fees page for the sponsorship leg; the route itself has no central portal or fee, so nothing more could be verified.

01

What it pays

  • Each post sets its own salary. No official figure exists for the route as a whole. The board's Mayo example is about $67-79k a year.
  • No application fee. If ECFMG sponsors your J-1, the sponsorship costs are $370 (annual) + $220 SEVIS + the J-1 visa fee.
  • ECFMG-sponsored scholars must be funded at $1,600 a month or more.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone with a conferred MBBS whom a host lab will take. Whether USMLE is needed depends on the host and was not confirmed.
  • Avoid unpaid posts. The route only works if the host pays you and sponsors the visa.

03

Dates that matter

  • Rolling all year. Posts open and close on their own dates.
  • The board's advice is to start emailing principal investigators in May-July 2027 for a post-internship start.
  • Allow time after an offer for the DS-2019 and the visa interview in Dhaka; processing times were not verified.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

For the 2029 Match this is the most useful thing you can do with 2027-28: US letters of recommendation, recent graduation and a salary that protects your $30,000. For Europe it only helps indirectly, as a stronger CV for a later funded MPH or PhD. It does not count towards any European licence.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no central route

    You find each post yourself. Mass emails get ignored, so each one must show you have read the lab's papers.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no publications yet

    You are competing with people who have papers. Any thesis, audit or case report from the internship helps.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: visa rules are unsettled

    The board's own tracking says the H-1B $100,000 fee is tied up in court and that university guidance (7 Oct, still current at the board's 1 Nov check) said it was not being collected; none of this is confirmed on the official fee pages, so treat it as unsettled. Cap-exempt university employers avoid the cap-subject fee issues, and J-1 via ECFMG is the safer leg.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: research is not clinical experience

    You will have little or no patient contact, and the time does not count as residency training. The two-year home rule may apply to a J-1 if US or Bangladeshi government funding is involved.

06

The honest recommendation

Make this your main plan for 2027-28. Use the internship year to build a CV, pick 20 to 30 labs in epidemiology and public health, and start writing in May-July 2027. Insist on a paid post and ask the host early which visa they use.

Not a job: it is the visa paperwork once a US lab has offered you a post

ECFMG sponsors J-1 visas for physicians doing research at US hosts that have no J-1 designation of their own. It only starts after a lab offers you a post, so the hard part is the offer, not the visa. Fees are small: about $750 for the first year.

Before you board

PortalECFMG EVSP, via MyIntealth (with your host's Training Program Liaison) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

ECFMG's annual application fee is $370 (required every case), plus SEVIS $220 and the J-1 visa application fee, listed at $160 on ECFMG's page. Re-check the visa fee against the State Department before paying. Extra $367 + $200 only for cases needing Department of State review (change of category, exceptional extension). Your host starts the process.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against ECFMG's EVSP Fees page (crawled 18 Apr 2026) and the EVSP Research Scholar checklist; the visa-fee line needs a re-check.

01

What it costs

  • $370 ECFMG annual application fee (every year of sponsorship), $220 SEVIS, and the J-1 visa fee, listed as $160 on ECFMG's page.
  • Special appeals, only if needed: $367 (State Department) + $200 (ECFMG).
  • Minimum funding for the exchange visitor is $1,600 a month. ECFMG does not pay you; the host does.

02

Who can apply

  • You, with a US host that has offered a research post and is working with ECFMG. Your host's Training Program Liaison coordinates the application, and you apply through MyIntealth.
  • The board's card says USMLE and ECFMG certification are generally not required for this category; confirm with ECFMG.

03

Dates that matter

  • Rolling, tied to the start date of the appointment. The $370 fee is annual.
  • Nothing to do until you hold an offer, which opens only after the MBBS is conferred.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

This is plumbing for the paid-research-post route, and it is the safest visa leg when the host cannot sponsor directly. It matters only for the US goal. A year on a J-1 research scholar visa builds the letters and research the Match looks for, but it does not count as clinical experience.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no offer, no sponsorship

    ECFMG does not find you a job.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no patient care

    The board describes the category as research with no or incidental patient contact, so check what your host plans.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: the two-year home rule

    It may apply if US or Bangladeshi government funding is involved. Ask your host before accepting.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: fees recur and move

    The $370 repeats each year and the visa fee line should be re-checked before you pay.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not spend time here yet. Read the EVSP checklist once so nothing surprises you, then put the effort into getting offers. Budget about $750 for year one and ask each host whether they sponsor directly or through ECFMG.

PortalMyIntealth (ECFMG) and the FSMB USMLE portal ↗ (opens in a new tab)

01

What it costs

  • ECFMG certification application $580. Step 1 $905 ($695 + $210 surcharge). Step 2 CK $930 ($695 + $235). Pathway application $945.
  • That is $3,360 in listed fees. OET Medicine, prep material, ERAS and the Match come on top.
  • All amounts are USD. Fees change each year and the April 2026 schedule applies to 2027.

02

Who can apply

  • Graduates of schools listed in WDOMS with an ECFMG sponsor note. Check your school's note on wdoms.org before paying for anything.
  • Register through FSMB for the exams and MyIntealth for certification.

03

Dates that matter

  • Exams run all year in three-month eligibility periods, so there is no single exam deadline.
  • 2027 Pathways close 31 Jan 2027; the 2028 season is not announced.
  • The 2027 Match is too early for you. Target 2028 or 2029. Step 2 CK is the score screen.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Everything in the US plan runs through this. For Europe it does nothing for licensing, though a strong Step 2 CK score still signals ability in an MPH or PhD application. With no licence, the board reads Pathway 6 (Mini-CEX) as the realistic clinical-skills option.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: sponsor note

    If your school's WDOMS sponsor note does not cover your graduation year, check with ECFMG before you pay.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: new exam format

    The board notes Step 1 and Step 2 CK now use 30-minute blocks. Practise with the new tutorial.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: the stack grows

    Add OET, a prep resource, a clinical placement and the Match. Keep a running budget.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: rules move

    The board is tracking visa and J-1 policy changes. Re-read ECFMG news before each payment.

06

The honest recommendation

Start Step 1 preparation during the internship, since it is the one step entirely in your hands. Do not pay the Pathway fee until the 2028 season opens and you know which Match year you are targeting.

Who can apply

Apply only if you are happy to put the 2029 Match at risk for a funded European year. If so, contact admissions about the MBBS route and GRE this week, request your marks and a class-rank letter now, and aim to complete the file well before 10 Dec.

Before you board

PortalNo central portal: contact NIH labs directly (OITE: training.nih.gov) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

NIH's official pages state no application fee, and there is no central application to pay for. Approaching principal investigators and registering with OITE are free. Once a lab selects you, NIH's Division of International Services processes the Visiting Program case and NIH sponsors the J-1 itself, not ECFMG. Government visa fees apply later.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against NIMH and NIAID training pages and NIH Division of International Services guidance; no fee stated, none found.

01

What it pays

  • A stipend scaled by experience. No official figure was verified.
  • No application fee stated. NIH sponsors your J-1; visa-stage government fees would apply.

02

Who can apply

  • A Visiting Fellow holds a doctoral degree with under five years of relevant postdoctoral experience. The board cites NIH policy as "PhD, MD or equivalent".
  • Whether your MBBS counts as MD-equivalent is not confirmed. Ask NIH's Division of International Services (DIS) before investing time.

03

Dates that matter

  • No deadline. Labs fill posts when they have an opening.
  • You cannot start before your MBBS is conferred, so think 2027-28.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

If it works, it is among the best CV lines for a US residency application: recent US research, an NIH letter and a paid year. It does nothing for a European licence. It is also open-ended, with the whole process decided by one lab's budget.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: eligibility is unconfirmed

    If NIH does not treat the MBBS as a doctoral degree, the route is closed.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: you do not apply to NIH centrally

    You apply to labs, and the lab chooses.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: no track record

    Fellows usually bring research experience; you have none yet.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: not clinical

    It does not count as US clinical experience.

06

The honest recommendation

Send one short email to DIS asking whether an MBBS qualifies. If yes, add NIH labs to the same outreach list as your other US posts. If no, you have lost nothing.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue (apply on each programme's site) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The catalogue is a directory, not an application portal. Each consortium sets its own fee and the great majority of Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters charge none, but that is not guaranteed. The programme's own site is the only authority. You may apply to at most three programmes per cycle.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against the EACEA Erasmus Mundus Catalogue page; no central fee exists.

01

What it pays

  • Scholarship holders pay no tuition and get a monthly allowance. The board's programme cards show about €1,400 a month for 24 months, with the exact terms set per programme.
  • Most programmes charge no application fee. This is not guaranteed, so check each site.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone with a bachelor's-level degree that the programme accepts. MBBS is accepted for health programmes but not all, so read each requirement.
  • Apply to at most three programmes.

03

Dates that matter

  • The EACEA page says most programmes take applications between October and January for the following September. Each consortium sets its own dates.
  • Individual cards on the board hold the exact dates for the programmes you are likely to pick.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Choose public health, epidemiology, nutrition, health data science or tropical medicine. They add a European credential and base, but a two-year master's starting in Sept 2027 overlaps your internship and moves the US Match back. Choose a one-programme shortlist rather than a scattergun.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: scholarship not guaranteed

    The catalogue warns that some listed programmes no longer offer Erasmus Mundus scholarships. Eu-HEM on this board is one.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: each programme is its own application

    Dates, documents and fees all differ.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: timeline

    A Sept 2027 start collides with the internship and delays the 2029 Match.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: no licence

    These are academic degrees, not routes to practise.

06

The honest recommendation

Use the catalogue to shortlist three programmes whose pages explicitly accept medicine, check each scholarship line, then apply to all three. Decide about the Sept 2027 clash only when you have an offer.

Before you board

PortalSOPHAS (most schools of public health); some use their own portal ↗ (opens in a new tab)

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each additional one. Some programmes add their own fee. Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's Least Developed Countries list, so you can request the international fee waiver, which covers the $155 first fee only; apply before you submit. Some schools, such as UNC Gillings' PhD, use their own portal.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against the SOPHAS Fees and Fee Waivers page on Liaison's Applicant Help Center.

01

What it pays

  • The funding comes from each university's own offer (tuition waiver plus stipend), not from SOPHAS. Terms differ per school, so read the offer.
  • Application fee: $155 first programme, $65 each extra. Bangladesh is on SOPHAS's Least Developed Countries list, so you can request the international fee waiver (limited and first-come; it covers the first $155 only, so apply before you submit).

02

Who can apply

  • An MBBS is usually accepted for direct entry. JHU Epidemiology needs TOEFL 100 / IELTS 7 and does not need the GRE. Harvard PHS requires the GRE.
  • UNC does not need the GRE; funding there is not guaranteed and files incomplete on 31 Jan are not reviewed.

03

Dates that matter

  • 1 Dec 2026 for JHU and Harvard (Harvard 5 pm). 15 Dec 2026 for UNC. JHU's PhD in Clinical Investigation closes 1 Mar 2027.
  • No single deadline: each programme page is the authority.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A PhD is a research-career route, not a faster way to residency. Four to six years of non-clinical work leaves you seven to nine years past graduation at Match time. It can bring a visa, US mentors and strong letters, but you cannot do it and the 2029 Match together.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: timing

    You would need test scores, three letters and a research statement within weeks.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no research record

    Admissions committees expect evidence of research ability.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Match conflict

    The PhD runs into the 2030s and weakens a clinical application.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: funding terms vary

    Department funding is not always guaranteed.

06

The honest recommendation

Apply only if you have genuinely decided that research matters more than the 2029 Match. If that is you, prepare JHU first, since it needs no GRE, and use the Bangladesh fee waiver. If the Match is the priority, skip it.

PortalKnight-Hennessy Scholars application, plus Stanford Graduate Admissions ↗ (opens in a new tab)

The KHS application is free, stated explicitly on KHS's official page. The separate Stanford graduate programme application costs $125, non-refundable, and KHS cannot waive it. Both applications are required. The 2027 cohort is closed.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against KHS's Your Applications and Online Application pages and Stanford Graduate Admissions' Application Fee page.

01

What it pays

  • KHS funds a Stanford graduate degree. Check the KHS site for the exact package, which was not re-verified here.
  • KHS charges no application fee. The Stanford programme application is $125.

02

Who can apply

  • You must be admitted to a Stanford graduate programme and also selected by KHS. Neither guarantees the other.
  • Your first bachelor's degree must have been received within the seven years before enrolment. A 2026 MBBS graduate qualifies, but the window is time-limited.

03

Dates that matter

  • 2027 cohort: opened 1 Jun 2026, closed 6 Oct 2026. The Stanford programme application was due by the earlier of its KHS deadline or 1 Dec 2026.
  • Next cohort (autumn 2028) would open about 1 Jun 2027 on the same annual pattern. This is not officially announced.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A funded Stanford degree is a strong signal, but it is academic, not clinical, and it does not change your Match timeline in your favour. The 2028 cohort fits after the internship, which is why it is worth keeping on the list.

05

The catches

  1. 01

  2. 02

  3. 03

    Catch 3: tiny acceptance

    KHS is highly selective; acceptance figures were not verified.

  4. 04

    KHS selects for leadership and civic engagement, which takes time to build.

Do not spend effort now. Use 2027 to build a leadership and research story, then check the KHS site in June 2027 for the 2028 cohort.

A clean fit after the internship, but a long process via the Ministry

The MEXT Research Student scholarship via the Embassy of Japan funds a master's or PhD in Japan. For Bangladesh the first step is the Ministry of Education's advert each April, then the Embassy. The round that fits you opens in April 2027 for April 2028 arrival, which matches the end of your internship.

✦ Drafted by Gemini (an AI), then rewritten and fact-checked against official pages on 2–3 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

Before you board

PortalNo online portal: Bangladesh Ministry of Education advert, then the Embassy of Japan ↗ (opens in a new tab)

No fee is stated on the Embassy page or the MEXT information it links to, and no official statement says there is none. The call is advertised each April by the Ministry of Education (moedu.gov.bd) and applications first go to the Ministry, which forwards shortlisted candidates to the Embassy. The Embassy distributes forms to selected candidates, returned in June.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against the Embassy of Japan in Bangladesh MEXT schedule page and basic-requirements PDF; fee not found.

01

What it pays

  • The board's card lists a funded package. The Embassy page checked does not state amounts, so confirm them in the April guidelines.
  • Application fee: not found.

02

Who can apply

  • Research Students (master's or PhD) under 35 who apply in their university major or a related field. The exact birth-date cutoff for your round appears only in the April 2027 guidelines.
  • A written exam and an interview at the Embassy are mandatory.

03

Dates that matter

  • The standing schedule: Ministry advert and application in April; shortlist to the Embassy in May; forms to the Embassy in June; written exam and interview in July; provisional selection in August; final MEXT selection in December; departure the following April.
  • The April 2027 departure round closed in April 2026. The next round opens April 2027 for April 2028 departure.
  • Exact dates appear only in the April advert on moedu.gov.bd.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Japanese master's or PhD is a research credential, not a clinical one. It means giving up years that the US Match would otherwise use. The April 2028 arrival fits cleanly after the internship, but only makes sense if you choose a research career over the 2029 Match.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: no direct applications

    The first stage is the Ministry, not the Embassy.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: exam and interview

    You must pass both at the Embassy.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: research plan

    You must apply in your own field or a related one, with a clear plan.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: Match conflict

    Years in Japan delay residency.

06

The honest recommendation

Keep it as a post-internship option. Watch moedu.gov.bd in April 2027 and prepare a research plan in public health or epidemiology now. Do not count on it unless you accept leaving the 2029 Match behind.

Window confirmed, but the requirement is a STEM bachelor's and medicine isn't named

imAGEin is an Erasmus Mundus master's in biomedical and computational sciences of ageing, run from Université Côte d'Azur. Applications run 6 Jan to 6 Mar 2027 and the course starts in the first week of September 2027. The catch is that it requires a STEM bachelor's of at least 180 ECTS, and medicine is not named.

Before you board

PortalUniversité Côte d'Azur eCandidat (link published at opening) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

No application fee, and no statement that there is none, appears on the programme's application page. Applications are entirely online through Université Côte d'Azur's eCandidat platform; the link is published from the opening date. Incomplete or late applications are not considered.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against the imAGEin Application & Registration page and the October 2026 brochure; fee not found.

01

What it pays

  • Erasmus Mundus scholarships of €1,400 a month are available for selected students (duration not stated on the page checked).
  • The self-funded fee was not confirmed in the verified pages. Application fee: not found.

02

Who can apply

  • A bachelor's in STEM (min. 180 ECTS) and proof of English: IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 93, or a certificate that your degree was taught in English.
  • Medicine isn't named. Email the programme and ask whether an MBBS counts. Final-year students may apply conditionally but must hold the degree before enrolment.

03

Dates that matter

  • Opens 6 Jan 2027, closes Saturday 6 Mar 2027. The final document list for 2027-29 was due to be confirmed from mid-October.
  • Programme starts the first week of September 2027.

A biomedical and computational master's could suit a health-data path, but ageing science is far from clinical practice and the September 2027 start overlaps your internship. It delays the US Match and gives no European licence.

  3. 03

The call normally runs Nov-Dec, but you need a supervisor first and the start clashes

Under MEXT University Recommendation, a Japanese university screens and nominates you. At Hamamatsu University School of Medicine the route is a doctoral degree with October entry, and the call normally runs November to December (the page says it may vary). You must have a supervisor before applying, and the October 2027 start overlaps your internship.

Before you board

PortalNo online portal: apply through the host department (Hamamatsu University School of Medicine) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

No MEXT application fee is stated. You must pass Hamamatsu's own graduate-school entrance examination at your own expense, and the examination fee is refunded after October if you are selected as a MEXT recipient. The fee amount is not published on the scholarship page. Other Japanese universities run their own calls.

How this was checked: Checked 3 Nov 2026 against Hamamatsu University School of Medicine's MEXT University Recommendation page; exam fee amount not found.

01

What it pays

  • ¥145,000 a month for four years, according to the Hamamatsu page. Airfare and other benefits were not confirmed.
  • No MEXT application fee is stated. Hamamatsu's entrance exam fee is paid up front and refunded after October if you are selected; the amount isn't published.

02

Who can apply

  • Generally aged 34 or younger, with a GPA of at least 2.30/3.0 and English at CEFR B2 in all four skills (or JLPT N2).
  • You must hold several online interviews with a prospective supervisor before applying. Once nominated you cannot withdraw, and applying to other universities or other Japanese-government scholarships in parallel is prohibited.

03

Dates that matter

  • Call for applications: Nov-Dec (may vary), applied for through the host department.
  • Internal screening results after early February; MEXT's final results in late June; October entry.
  • The page describes October admission only; you could ask whether a later start is possible to avoid the internship overlap.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

This is a four-year doctoral research route in Japan, so it takes you out of the 2029 Match. It might suit a research career in public health or epidemiology, but it does nothing for US or European licensing.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: supervisor first

    Without interviews and a supervisor, you cannot apply.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: the window is short

    If the call follows the usual Nov-Dec pattern, you have weeks to act.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: you pay the exam first

    The refund only comes if you are selected.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: timeline

    An Oct 2027 start clashes with the internship by about a month.

06

The honest recommendation

Only worth pursuing if you are ready to commit four years to a Japanese PhD. If so, email Hamamatsu departments this week. Otherwise, let it pass and keep the Embassy route in mind for April 2027.

Before you board

PortalDAAD Portal (link appears only while a call is running) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Register on the DAAD Portal and upload documents under 'Attachments'. DAAD states no charge for applying. You must also win admission to a German master's yourself, and DAAD does not pay tuition at the host university.

How this was checked: DAAD scholarship database entry for the Master's Study Scholarship (Application Procedure and Submitting an Application tabs), 3 Nov 2026; the fee is listed as NOT FOUND, but no charge is mentioned anywhere on the page.

01

What it pays

  • EUR 992 a month, plus health, accident and liability insurance.
  • A EUR 460 yearly study allowance and a travel allowance.
  • DAAD does not cover tuition; check the host university's own fees.
  • Funding runs 10 to 24 months, only with admission to the named host university.

02

Who can apply

  • Graduates with a first degree finished by the start of funding and, as a rule, no more than 6 years old at the deadline.
  • No professional-experience requirement is listed on the programme page (EPOS, by contrast, needs at least 2 years).
  • You must arrange your own admission to a full-time master's at a German university.
  • You cannot apply if you have lived in Germany more than 15 months at the deadline.

03

Dates that matter

  • 1 Jun to 31 Aug 2026: Bangladesh window, now closed (selection Feb 2027, funding from Oct 2027).
  • DAAD updates deadlines every spring and they are country-specific, so re-check the programme page.
  • The next call is not published; if the usual yearly pattern holds it would be for funding from October 2028 (not confirmed).

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

For Europe this is the best-fitting funded master's you have: two years in Germany to reach B2 and C1 medical German, then Approbation. A funded start from October 2028 would also come after your internship, which a 2027 start would not.

For the US, a master's adds research and letters but takes 1 to 2 years. It does not replace Step 1, a paid research job or Step 2 CK, so Match 2029 would move to about 2030.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: it has closed

    There is no way into the 2027 round now.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: two applications

    You need German admission and a DAAD award; neither guarantees the other.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: a master's is not a licence

    Approbation is a separate process with its own exams.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: the 6-year rule

    It runs from your degree, so delay beyond about 2032 costs eligibility.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not chase this cycle. Use 2027 to pick two or three German master's, get a research output, and be ready to apply the moment the next Bangladesh window opens.

A means-tested benefit you claim after an Italian place, not a prize

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: your region's right-to-study agency (example ER.GO, Emilia-Romagna) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

DSU is claimed online from the regional agency for the region where your university sits, under that agency's yearly call. Non-EU students also complete pre-enrolment on Universitaly for admission and visa. The family papers (ISEE parificato, legalised and translated) cost money to prepare, but no fee for the claim itself is mentioned.

How this was checked: ER.GO guide to the 2026/27 call, UNIMORE and University of Parma fee pages, 3 Nov 2026; no fee found and the 2027/28 deadlines are NOT FOUND (regional calls appear in summer 2027).

01

What it pays

  • About EUR 7,171 or more a year in cash, per the board card.
  • Full or partial university fee exemption, canteen access and accommodation (as the region provides).
  • It is paid by the region, so it varies by agency (ER.GO, DiSCo, EDISU and others).

02

Who can apply

  • Students enrolled or pre-enrolled at a public Italian university.
  • Family income and assets under the regional ceilings; the board card lists ISEE up to EUR 28,339.88 and ISPE up to EUR 61,608.48 for 2026/27.
  • As a Bangladeshi you need an ISEE parificato, with income and asset documents legalised and translated.
  • Later years need a minimum number of credits.

03

Dates that matter

  • Regional calls for 2027/28 appear in summer 2027 (ER.GO publishes around July).
  • Benefit deadlines usually fall in late summer or autumn.
  • Italian university admission and Universitaly pre-enrolment come first.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

It can make an Italian master's close to free, which protects your USD 30,000 for exams and US rotations. But the degree takes about two years and would push Match from 2029 to roughly 2030 or later.

It does not license you in Italy. Recognition of your MBBS and Italian language are separate steps.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: not a competition

    It is a means-tested claim, not a prize; you may apply while pre-enrolled, but you need an Italian university place to use it.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: paperwork

    Legalising and translating Bangladeshi family papers takes months, so start early.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: credits

    Keeping the money needs study progress, which competes with USMLE preparation.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: region matters

    The portal, call and deadline depend on the region of your chosen university.

06

The honest recommendation

Treat DSU as a cost-saver for an Italian master's you already want, not a reason to go to Italy. Choose the course first, then check that region's call.

EURAXESS says no charges apply to its Jobs portal, and universities do not charge for advertised salaried posts. You apply to each vacancy through the employer. These are jobs, so each post sets its own closing date and degree rules.

How this was checked: EURAXESS 'About EURAXESS', Jobs and member-apply terms, 3 Nov 2026; there is no central deadline (NOT FOUND) because every vacancy has its own.

01

A paid PhD abroad is excellent for research, but at 3 to 4 years it replaces the 2029 plan rather than adding to it. For Europe it gives residence and language time, but you still need local licensing.

Before you board

Portaluni-assist: Pay & submit (many German universities); others apply direct ↗ (opens in a new tab)

On the uni-assist route the fee is EUR 75 for the first course and EUR 30 for each additional course, per application semester, and it is charged again if you reapply. Some uni-assist universities cover the fee. Universities that take direct applications set their own arrangements and many charge nothing. Semester contributions, a blocked account and living costs are separate.

How this was checked: Checked uni-assist's Pay & submit and handling-fees page on 3 Nov 2026; no single national deadline or direct-route fee exists, so those are NOT FOUND.

01

What it costs

  • Tuition is usually nil at public universities, but not everywhere: Baden-Wurttemberg charges non-EU students tuition, per the verified notes.
  • You still pay semester contributions, living costs and a blocked account for the visa. The board estimates about USD 16-18k in year 1 and about USD 30k over two years.
  • uni-assist fee: EUR 75 plus EUR 30 per extra course.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone with a recognised degree that meets the programme's own entry rules. Check each programme page for the public health or statistics background it asks for.
  • Whether a given programme uses uni-assist, the VPD pre-check or its own portal must be read on that programme's page.
  • English-taught programmes need English proof; check each programme's language rules.

03

Dates that matter

  • No national deadline. Typical German master's windows are around 15 January for summer starts and 15 July for winter starts, but each programme sets its own.
  • uni-assist says document checks take weeks, so apply early.
  • A winter 2027 start would overlap your internship; the board's date is about 15 Jan 2028 for a summer 2028 start.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

This is your one fully realistic way to a European degree on a USD 30,000 budget, but it spends most of that budget. A two-year degree starting 2027 or 2028 would also take you away from the 2029 Match timetable and give no US clinical experience.

A master's is not a medical licence; German medical licensing is a separate process that the verified notes do not cover.

  1. 01

    Catch 1: Budget

    Two years of living costs take about your whole USD 30k, leaving little for USMLE fees, electives and ERAS.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: Match timing

    A degree running to 2029 or 2030 makes your graduation year older and gives no US clinical experience.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Not a licence

    A master's is not a medical licence; licensing is a separate process.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: Deadlines vary

    There is no single date, so every programme must be checked on its own page.

06

The honest recommendation

Keep it as a funded-by-yourself Plan B for Europe. Short-list two or three English-taught programmes now, price them, and decide after you see your Step 1 plan. Do not commit the USD 30k until the US route is clearer.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: DHA Sheryan, DOH TAMM, MOHAP ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Three separate authorities: Dubai (DHA, Sheryan), Abu Dhabi (DOH, TAMM) and the northern emirates (MOHAP). DHA credentialing is AED 200; DOH application AED 100 plus DataFlow PSV AED 1,260 for GPs; MOHAP evaluation AED 500 then AED 100. Exam fees (Prometric or Pearson VUE) are not published as fixed amounts, and licence fees are normally paid by the hiring facility.

How this was checked: Checked DHA Sheryan service pages, DOH TAMM and Licensing Manual (Circular 151/2024) and MOHAP service pages on 3 Nov 2026; no application window or exam fee exists, so those are NOT FOUND.

01

What it costs

  • Staged government fees: DHA credentialing AED 200; DOH AED 100 plus DataFlow AED 1,260 for GPs; MOHAP evaluation AED 500 plus AED 100.
  • Licence fees (for example DOH AED 2,500 for a year) are paid when a facility activates your licence. Exam fees are not published as fixed amounts.

02

Who can apply

  • All three authorities use shared Professional Qualification Requirements: qualification plus post-internship experience for a GP title.
  • The number of years is not stated in the verified notes; the board's note of about two years is unconfirmed.
  • An individual cannot hold a practising licence without a hiring facility.

03

Dates that matter

  • No application window or deadline; licensing is a rolling government service.
  • Registration must be activated by a facility within its validity (for example DHA, one year).
  • Your earliest realistic date is after you have completed the required experience.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A Gulf licence is a salary-earning fallback. It does not help USMLE and it gives no US clinical experience. Working there for two years first also takes the time you need for Steps and the 2029 Match.

A UAE licence is not a European licence.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: Experience gate

    Fresh graduates may not qualify for the GP title. Check the current PQR before paying anything.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: Three licences

    A licence from one authority does not cover the others, though transfers are possible.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: Job first

    You need a licensed facility to employ you before the licence is issued.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: Fees staged

    Exam and DataFlow fees can change, so use only the amount shown at checkout.

06

The honest recommendation

Do not pay for DataFlow or exams now. Keep this as a later Plan B, and re-read the PQR in 2028 when your experience position is clear.

Who can apply

For Europe it adds a research line to your CV and nothing more. It does not shorten any licensing route.

The only fixed cost is $155 for the first SOPHAS programme, and a limited number of fee waivers go to citizens and residents of UN Least Developed Countries (Bangladesh is on the list).

Before you board

PortalSOPHAS (MPH programmes); US research jobs have no central portal ↗ (opens in a new tab)

SOPHAS charges $155 for the first programme and $65 for each extra one, and some programmes add a supplemental fee. A limited number of waivers go to citizens and residents of UN Least Developed Countries (Bangladesh is on the list), first come first served, covering only the first $155. Job applications carry no standard fee.

How this was checked: Checked the SOPHAS fees and waivers page (Liaison help centre) on 3 Nov 2026; no single scheme deadline exists, each programme sets its own.

01

What it pays and costs

  • SOPHAS: $155 first programme, $65 each extra, and some programmes add a supplemental fee.
  • A limited number of waivers cover the first $155 for citizens and residents of UN Least Developed Countries. Bangladesh is on the list. First come, first served.
  • MPH funding is decided school by school. Job pay is set by each employer. Neither amount is published centrally.

02

Who can apply

  • Anyone applying to a SOPHAS programme. Each school sets its own requirements.
  • The model is a personal account relayed on the board, not an official source, and its details are not verified here.

03

Dates that matter

  • There is no scheme deadline. Each programme sets its own within the cycle.
  • Example from the verified flags: Hopkins Bloomberg MPH closes 1 Dec 2026 for July 2027 and waives its work-experience rule for foreign medical graduates. Georgia State's priority deadline is 15 Feb 2027, with limited, non-guaranteed assistantships.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Classes starting mid-2027 clash with an internship that runs to about late 2027, so most realistic starts are 2028. A one-year MPH then ends around mid-2029, after the September 2028 ERAS window, which makes 2029 hard and 2030 more likely. It still builds Step 1 time, US research jobs and letters.

For Europe it supports public health or research roles, not clinical licensing.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: funding is not guaranteed

    Assistantships and scholarships vary by programme.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: timing

    The internship overlaps the 2027 intake and the degree pushes the Match later.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: US cost of living

    Tuition gaps and living costs can use up $30,000 fast without a campus job.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: F-1 work limits

    Job rules depend on the visa, so check before you rely on income.

06

The honest recommendation

It is one of the few routes here you largely control. Apply to a short list of MPH programmes with fee waivers requested, and decide the start year only after seeing which offers come with real money.

BCS is a Bangladesh career route, not a licensing step. The exam, results and posting stages take years, and a government post leaves little time for USMLE study or US clinical experience. It makes sense only as a safety net if the 2029 Match plan fails.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

Part I does not count for ECFMG, USMLE or any European regulator. Its value is as a low-cost Bangladesh fallback. The basic-science revision overlaps Step 1, but the exam is its own format. Full FCPS training is a multi-year, full-time commitment that conflicts with the 2029 Match.

  • Not available for study in the United Kingdom or Russia.

How it fits the US and Europe goals

  2. 02

Over budget on its own: a self-funded UK master's is a dead end without help

A self-funded UK one-year master's is just ordinary entry to a university course, paid in full by you. International tuition plus UK living costs are likely well above a USD 30,000 budget on their own, which is why the board marks it closed to you. Apply direct to each university; deadlines are set per course.

✦ Drafted by Gemini (an AI), then rewritten and fact-checked against official pages on 2–3 Nov 2026. Where they disagreed, the official page won.

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: apply direct to each UK university (UCAS postgraduate hub) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

Postgraduate courses are applied for directly to each provider. Some universities charge a per-application fee (Glasgow lists £25 for its MBA only); many charge nothing. Most ask for a £1,000 to £2,000+ deposit before issuing a visa document.

How this was checked: UCAS's postgraduate pages and Glasgow's fees page were checked on 3 Nov 2026; no umbrella fee exists.

01

What it costs

  • Full international tuition plus living costs. We did not verify any specific course fee.
  • A deposit, commonly £1,000 to £2,000+, is usually needed to get your visa document.
  • Application fees vary, and many universities charge none.

02

Who can apply

  • Direct application to each university's own system.
  • Entry rules, English scores and deadlines are per course.

03

Dates that matter

  • UCAS advises applying by June or July for a September start, and at least six months ahead.
  • Competitive and scholarship-linked deadlines close much earlier, often Oct 2026 to Jan 2027.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

A UK master's could help for non-clinical European work, but it does not license you and it eats the budget the US exam route needs. Graduate visa rules were not checked here, so read gov.uk before relying on them.

05

The catches

  1. 01

    Catch 1: cost

    Fees plus living costs are likely to exceed your USD 30,000 (no course fee was verified).

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no umbrella figures

    Every fee and deadline must be read per university.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: deposit risk

    A £1,000 to £2,000+ deposit is paid before visa and funding are final.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: licensing

    A master's does not give GMC registration or reduce USMLE steps.

06

The honest recommendation

Skip it unless you land a funded place elsewhere. If you want a UK master's, look at funded routes (Chevening later, GREAT) rather than paying the full fee.

UQ's Graduate Research School Scholarships (UQGRSS, including the Australian Government's Research Training Program) fund PhD and MPhil students with a tax-free stipend of AUD 39,220 a year (2026 rate) plus OSHC. There is one application with no separate scholarship form. The board earlier showed a round closing 19 Oct 2026, which we could not confirm; check UQ's scholarship page for current round dates.

What it pays

Before you board

PortalNo single portal: apply to each EPOS course directly (DAAD database entry) ↗ (opens in a new tab)

DAAD states no application fee of its own. Each course runs its own admission procedure, so any course-level charge is set by the university and is not stated on daad.de. Applications sent straight to DAAD are not forwarded to courses.

How this was checked: Checked the DAAD (daad.de) EPOS scholarship database entry on 3 Nov 2026; no DAAD fee stated, course-level fees not found.

01

What it pays

  • A development-related master's at a German university. The board lists a stipend of EUR 992 a month, but the official page checked does not state the amount.
  • The official page checked did not set out the full package, so confirm it on the course page.
  • No DAAD application fee is stated.

02

Who can apply

  • A bachelor's degree and at least 2 years of professional experience after the first degree.
  • You apply to up to three courses, each directly. Only candidates a course proposes are later asked to upload a full application to the DAAD portal.
  • Whether a compulsory internship counts is not stated on the page checked. Assume it does not until a course confirms.

03

Dates that matter

  • There is no single deadline. Each course sets its own.
  • DAAD publishes a list of all postgraduate courses with deadlines for 2027/28 (PDF on static.daad.de).
  • Earliest realistic application is after about two years of relevant work. Whether internship time counts is not stated.

04

How it fits the US and Europe goals

  • This is a good fit for your public health interest and a respectable European credential. It does nothing for USMLE, gives no US clinical experience, and a non-clinical master's does not license you in Germany.
  • A year in Germany on this route would also sit across the 2029 Match window. Treat it as a later option, not a 2029 plan.

05

  1. 01

    Catch 1: experience gate

    Two years after your first degree. You have none yet.

  2. 02

    Catch 2: no central application

    Each course has its own form, fee and deadline.

  3. 03

    Catch 3: not a licence

    A non-clinical master's does not itself license you to practise in Germany; that is a separate process.

  4. 04

    Catch 4: no US benefit

    It gives no US clinical experience and no USMLE preparation.
